Public Comment
During this time, members of the public or staff may address the Parks & Recreation
Commission regarding any items within the subject matter jurisdiction of the Commission.
Comments from the audience will be limited to three minutes per speaker; unless authorized
by the Commission Chair, the time limit may not be extended by utilizing another member's
time. There will be no debate or action on items not listed on the agenda unless authorized by
law. NOTE: Obscene language, comments intended to disrupt or interfere with the progress of
the meeting, or slanderous comments will not be tolerated and may result in ejection and/or
may constitute a violation of South Gate Municipal Code Section 1.04.110.

   Parks & Recreation Commission
  Regular Meeting Minutes
  August 8, 2024

CALL TO ORDER Vice Chair Ruiz called the meeting to order at 7:02 p.m.

FLAG SALUTE - by Secretary Pelayo

ROLL CALL - by Yodit Glaze, City Clerk
Present: Vice Chair Lizette Ruiz, Secretary Edgar Pelayo and Commissioners Cyntia Esquivel and Alejanda
Flores. Chair Flores had an excused absence.
Staff: Director Steve Costley, Parks Superintendent Glenn Massey, and Recreation Manager James Markel.

APPROVAL OF MEETING MINUTES FOR JULY 11, 2024
Recommended Motion: Motion to approve the minutes as presented
M/S/C: Secretary Pelayo/Commissioner Esquivel to approve the minutes as presented.
PUBLIC COMMENTS
Recognized: Leticia Vasquez Wilson, Representative the Central Water Basin, brought information
regarding the Water Basin's water conservation efforts.

PRESENTATION
ORAL REPOR OF PARK SECURITY BY SG POLICE DEPARTMENT
Director Costley clarified that once a year the PD will come so that the Commissioners may ask any
questions/concerns . Lt. Corella reported there have been no major issues at SG Park, police continue to
do routine patrols; cite people smoking or smoking marijuana, The gambling is addressed as they come
across it. They have been cited and they disburse but after while they return. Commissioner Esquivel
noticed more drinking and marijuana at the outdoor basketball courts
Is it possible to get more patrolling? Lt. Corella is in contact with the Park Rangers and try to coordinate
more patrolling but staff is limited. Vice Chair Ruiz stated that last year there was a stabbing at Hollydale
Regional Park restroom have there been other significant incidents and if so, what is being done to curtail
these issues. Director Costley said that after speaking with the PD it was decided to close the restrooms
and only open for special events. Secretary Pelayo asked if the non-emergency Police Department number
could be added to the signs; Parks Supt. Massey would look into it.

OPEN SESSION ITEMS

1. REVIEW OF RECREATION 4TH QUARTER REPORT FY 2023/24
Recommended Motion: Motion to receive and file.
M/S/C: Secretary Pelayo/Commissioner Flores
Recreation Mgr. Markel reviewed this item; a discussion ensued.

2. REVIEW OF GROUNDS & FACILITY MAINTENANCE 4TH QUARTER REPORT FY 2023/24
Recommended Motion: Motion to receive and file.
M/S/C: Commissioner Flores/Commissioner Esquivel
Parks Supt. Massey reviewed this item; a discussion ensued. Secretary Pelayo asked regarding the
sprinklers what is the area that gets damaged more often; the different types of damages were explained
by Parks Supt. Massey. Vice Chair Ruiz asked about flooding at the dog park; it was explained that it was a
broken sprinkler that was flooding the area.

  Page 1 of 2
  4
 3. UPDATE ON PARKS & RECREATION DEPARTMENT MAJOR PROJETS
Recommended Motion: Motion to receive and file.
M/S/C: Secretary Pelayo/ Vice Chair Ruiz
Director Costley spoke on the Auditorium roof project, the Boy Scout Huts, SG Park North Playground
Resurfacing, Circle Park, Hollydale Community Park, SG Park Fence, Urban Orchard; Recreation Mgr.
Markel spoke on the Sports Center/Swim Stadium projects. A discussion ensued. Secretary Pelayo

4. PROPOSED HALLOWEEN 2024 ACTIVITIES
Recommended Motion: Motion to accept the proposed activities.
M/S/C: Secretary Pelayo/Commissioner Flores
Recreation Mgr. Markel reviewed this item; a discussion ensued. Director Costley asked the
Commissioners to participate by being the judges for the costume contests. Commissioner Flores asked if
adults were included in the contest; staff will look into including adults. Vice Chair Ruiz voiced that she has
enjoyed being a judge and looking forward to the new activities.

DIRECTOR'S REPORT / CALENDAR OF EVENTS
Director Costley: Final Concerts in the Park had 400 in attendance for the Mariachi Divas. Movies in the
Park will begin with the movie Haunted Mansion. The Police Department Car Show will be held on
September 29 at the Golf Course. The LA Philharmonic will be in the Auditorium on September 25.

Parks Supt. Massey: Summer is the busiest time with the special events and high use . Staff has begun the
renovation of the soccer field at Hollydale Regional Park.

Recreation Mgr. Markel: The Fun Run had about 1,000 participants. Family Camp Night was very successful
with all 25 spots sold out; great reviews on all the activities. Up coming special events, Zine Festival at the
Art Gallery has begun; Movies in the Park has had close to 300 people and Tampico, Celsius, to name a few
are giving away drinks.

PARKS & RECREATION COMMISSION SUB-COMMITTEE REPORTS
Vice Chair Ruiz: Has Park attendance increased since Salt Lake Park in Huntington Park has had delays in
their playground repairs; Director Costley replied that it's difficult to judge because we usually have a
higher attendance in the summer.

Secretary Pelayo: None

Commissioner Esquivel: Asked if shade covers will be installed at Diamonds 9 & 10; Director Costley
replied that at present there isn't any funding.

Commissioner Flores: None

REQUEST FOR ITEMS ON FUTURE AGENDAS - None

ADJOURNMENT - At 8:08 p.m. Vice Chair Ruiz asked for a motion to adjourn.
M/S/C: Secretary Pelayo/Commissioner Flores

Respectfully submitted:

Edgar Pelayo, Secretary

   Parks & Recreation Commission Regular Meeting
  September 12, 2024
  STAFF REPORT ITEM No. 2
To:  Honorable Parks & Recreation Commission
From:  James Markel, Recreation Manager
Date:  August 21, 2024

Subject:  Annual Sports and Aquatics Division Report

Recommended Motion:  Motion to Receive and File

Report Summary:

Aquatics
The Aquatics Division experienced another dynamic year in 2023-2024. Our commitment to
enhancing community well-being, improving facilities, and expanding program offerings has led
to notable achievements across all seasons.
In Summer of 2023, we expanded our hours and programs. The Patricia G. Mitchell Swim
Stadium was open seven days a week for Lap, Adult, and Family Swim. We also grew our
Splash Membership program, with about 1,500 reoccurring monthly memberships. Our most
popular program, Learn-to-Swim, offering Group, Private, and Semi-Private swim lessons for all
ages, was at full capacity every month. We offered several therapy and fitness classes for
adults and seniors, such as: SeniorCise, Aqua Aerobics, Masters Swim, and Open Play Water
Polo. We featured specialized and aquatic sports programs like Junior Water Polo, Pre-Comp,
and hosted competitive swim teams South Gate Aquatics Club (SGAC), Penguins Aquatic Club
(PAC), and Lynwood Marlins (LMST). Special this summer was the launch of new programs
such as the Summer Splash Camp for Kids, Junior Lifeguard, Surfing 101, Surf Camp for
Teens, and Gators Swim Academy, with over 200 participants. We also expanded summer
aquatic fitness classes to include Aqua Blast, a higher intensity aqua aerobics class.

We continued to engage with our community with a variety of free water safety awareness
events. We partnered with SGAC and organized the World’s Largest Swimming Lesson in June
and had almost 200 participants. We also launched our free Community Swim Day series:
Summer Kick-Off Splash event in June, 4th of July Splash event in July, and Back-to-School
Splash event in August. Each event brought in over 100 participants. The theme of events was
to teach the community how to stay safe in and around the water and other ways to beat the
summer heat. Guests enjoyed lawn games, music, and prizes plus free entry to a bonus Family
Swim session offered that day.

Our Learn-to-Swim program and aquatic fitness classes continued through the fall, as did the
warm season, so we were still pretty busy. We were at capacity every month in the fall. We
continued to host partner organization South Gate Aqua Coalition (SGAC), Penguins Aquatic

  16
 Club (PAC) and Lynwood Marlins Swim Team (LMST). The Patricia G. Mitchell Swim Stadium is
also the “home pool” for the South-Central Swim League’s fall, winter, and spring seasons,
hosting approximately six meets per season. Each individual meet brings in about six local swim
teams, 400 local competitive swimmers, and over 600 spectators. This fall was extra special
because we rolled out a new event that is unlike anything we’ve ever done before: Patti’s
Pumpkin Plunge, a floating pumpkin patch! We featured arts and crafts, a pumpkin decorating
contest, games, prizes, music and more. We were sold out for both sessions and had 200
participants.

Come winter, things slowed down. The colder season brought new opportunities. We launched
a new membership program called Splash Fitness. This membership tier provides access to all
our recreational swim sessions and aquatic fitness classes at an economical price. As one of
the only indoor pools open year-round, we were able to continue hosting local swim teams’
practices, the South-Central Swim League’s winter swim league, SGAC’s USA Invitational 2-day
swim meet, and our adult and lap swimmers. We also offered our 11th Annual Youth Swim
Clinic, designed for novice and advanced competitive swimmers to improve their technique,
endurance, and speed. We had almost 100 youth register; currently our best feeder programs
for both club and high school swim and water polo teams. Inspired by the success of the
Halloween event, the Aquatics Team launched a special holiday event: Surfing with Santa. This
special day featured arts and crafts, games, activities, prizes, and an opportunity to surf with
Santa, Mrs. Claus, and their elves.

After the holidays, the pool took a break to focus on much needed facility and pool renovations.
The pool was drained in order to repair the wrinkles in the liner, a lane line anchor that was torn
out, and missing tiles around the pool bottom and walls. The Aquatics Staff also took this
opportunity to deep clean the patron locker-rooms, staff areas, deck, and patio. Staff also
created a few YouTube videos to help patrons become better aware of our programs and how
to register for them online.

In Spring 2024, the pool started to see more traffic as everyone starts prepping for the summer
season. Our most popular programs, Learn-to-Swim Group, Private, and Semi-Private swim
lessons for all ages were back. We offered a variety of safety training courses for the
community. In March, we held three different Adult and Pediatric First Aid/CPR/AED courses
with almost 30 participants. We also held three different Lifeguard Certification courses. As first
responders, Aquatics Staff is consistently training, and in May-June held our annual
recertification course certifying 50 Lifeguards in American Red Cross Lifeguarding with
CPR/AED For Professional Rescuers, First Aid, Administering Emergency Oxygen, and
Bloodborne Pathogens Training. May is designated as National Water Safety Month, so the
Swim Stadium in partnership with the Parks & Rec Social Media Team campaigned all month
long to bring water safety awareness to the community. We celebrated International Water
Safety Day on May 15 and hosted our 5th Annual Water Safety Bash, attracting over 100
participants.

Fitness
The Sports Center Fitness membership program had a robust start to the new year. Total
memberships grew to over 3,500 participants with almost 4,000 daily admissions coming in
during the 1st quarter. This momentum continued into the 2nd and 3rd quarters with our
membership database surpassing over 4,000 members during the start of 2024. New Year’s
resolutions and people wanting more active lifestyles usually account for an increase in
memberships during January through March. By the 4th quarter, we had over 4,400
memberships and processed 4,498 daily admissions. Overall, membership registrations grew

  17
 25% from first to fourth quarters.

The introduction of new Group Exercise classes has been well-received by members. The new
Zumba classes on Tuesdays and Thursdays from 11:15 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. continue to be very
popular. Our Senior Fitness Programs: Seniorcise and Over Easy have increased their
attendance by 100%. Staff has worked hard to develop age-appropriate exercises and
programs that keep our Seniors engaged and motivated. We added a new Outdoor Yoga class
that immediately drew significant interest from members. During the warmer seasons, there will
be as many as 50 people practicing their yoga poses and breathing techniques under the
beautiful South Gate Park trees. Currently, the Sports Center offers a diverse range of over 30
fitness classes weekly that cater to all members and their preferences.

Youth Fitness Programming continued to flourish, with Youth Olympic Weightlifting and
Basketball Training Sessions reaching near maximum capacity every session. These popular
programs attract many participants, thanks to their focus on enhancing muscular development
and coordination. Our highly sought after Biggest Loser program, which is celebrating its 10-
year anniversary, has once again reached full capacity. Over the course of 12 long grueling
weeks, participants challenge themselves every day through a variety of staff led resistance
training sessions and workouts. There are weekly weigh-ins with opportunities to win prizes for
weight loss and participation.
The Personal Training Program experienced growth, with a total of 884 hours of training
conducted over the fiscal year. Notably, there was a huge increase in the Private 12-session
packages, with 384 hours conducted this year compared to last year's 264 hours. This can be
attributed to clients entrusting their Certified Personal Trainers to achieve their fitness goals and
dedicating the time to continue training with staff. The semi-private 16-session package also
increased, recording 288 hours of training. To meet the rising demand, we have expanded our
team with more certified trainers. The program remains highly requested and continues to
receive excellent feedback from clients.

In January, we held our Annual Sports Center Open House, which was open to the public and
showcased all the facilities and fitness programming available. The event featured abbreviated
versions of Group Exercise classes, Personal Training Assessments, and enjoyable sports
activities for the entire family. Attendees also had the chance to win prizes through staff-led
activities throughout the day.

Our Spring Fit 5K returned for its 7th year. Bimbo Bakeries once again served as the title
sponsor, providing 800 performance tech shirts to all registered participants. The party started
at 6:00 a.m. with a DJ playing the latest hits. The Children’s Play Area had more inflatables, and
activities to win prizes. The accompanying vendor fair, featuring various sponsors offering
products and goodies, was also a major highlight. The Spring Fit 5K remains a cornerstone
event for our department and is set to grow even larger in the future.

The 3rd Annual Fun Run took place on July 20. The one-mile park course was filled with
inflatable obstacles, water slides, slime, foam, and mud zones. This year, Home Depot's
generous donations allowed us to build more elaborate obstacles, and Amazon came on board
as a major sponsor, providing high-performance tech shirts for all participants. The event
included a vibrant vendor fair with Dirty Worms, Dunkin' Donuts, Tampico, Celsius, and Amazon
leading the way. With such strong support, the Fun Run is set to continue growing alongside our
other major events.

Youth Sports

  18
 Fiscal Year 2023-2024 was a very busy and successful year for our Youth Sports division.
Summer 2023 kicked off with our main Fundamental classes filling to capacity (Basketball,
Baseball, Soccer, Volleyball, and Multi-Sport). Classes met for 45 minutes, once a week, for
nine consecutive weeks. Every class culminated with live scrimmages, a group potluck, and
certificate presentations. Karate and Tennis contract classes were also offered during the
Summer and remained at capacity.

Fall 2023 continued steadily after an action-packed summer session. Our main offerings
remained the same with all classes filling to capacity again. Karate instructor Juan Larios hosted
his Annual International Karate-Do Shito-Ryu Federation Tournament on September 17 in the
Sports Center Gymnasium. Over 75 athletes from all regions competed to be named the
champion, and over 400 spectators attended throughout the tournament. We continued our
partnership with Special Olympics as their host site for their Fall 2023 games. We had over 500
Special Olympic athletes competing in Softball, Soccer, Volleyball, and Golf with hundreds of
spectators in attendance.

Winter 2024 experienced a slight decline in registration which is typical during the winter months
due to extreme weather and temperature changes. Once again, our offerings remained the
same and classes reached near full capacity. We hosted our annual Azalea Karate Tournament
on March 10. Additionally, we offered a weeklong baseball camp from March 25 through March
29 for participants ages 5 - 12 years old. Lastly, new to our Youth Sports division was the Glow
in the Dark Pickel ball event held in the Sports Center Gymnasium. Staff decorated the gym with
a variety of glow in the dark tape, paint, and equipment to create this spectacular pickleball
venue. The family event was held on Friday, March 29 from 6:30 p.m. to 9:00 p.m. and we had
over 75 participants.
Spring 2024 had classes return to full capacity. We brought back our popular Intermediate
Volleyball Fundamentals on Tuesday evenings. Our Youth Sports Division held its second
Basketball All-Star Skills Challenge. Participants competed in timed drills that showcased their
ball handling, passing, shooting, and agility skills. There were three age divisions (7-8, 9-10, &
11-12 year olds); the top finisher in each age division received an Under Armour basketball
backpack accompanied by a brand new Wilson basketball. To end our Spring quarter, Special
Olympics chose the South Gate Sports Center as their host site for their Annual Special
Olympics Basketball Competition. The event took place on June 1 and had 50 Special Olympic
athletes and over 200 spectators in attendance to support their athletes.

Adult Sports
Our Adult Softball leagues were able to complete 2 full seasons this year. Our Men’s league
takes place on Thursday evenings and had an overall total of 44 teams while Co-ed continued
its play on Friday evenings and had a total of 48 teams. Prizes for first place varied by season;
summer introduced our new championship tank tops and fall/spring received redesigned
championship hoodies. Second place prizes were also upgraded as they received customized
City of South Gate Softball water bottles. We continue to increase the number of teams per
season, and we are almost back to pre-pandemic numbers.

Adult Basketball will return this Fall. Our Men’s league will be playing on Friday nights, and we
are currently recruiting for a Women’s Basketball league as well.

Open Play Volleyball continues to be a popular program on Tuesday evenings, accounting for
over 2,500 drop-in participants during the past fiscal year. Adult Volleyball will look to
commence its inaugural season this Fall. Our Coed league will play on Tuesday nights from
6:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m.
